The Petitioners have filed this petition against Respondents for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989.

SCCH 5 2. The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 08.11.2023 at about 6.20 p.m. Lohith K.N. had been proceeding on motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01- EE-8375 near Kalavase Farm, NH-173 Road,
Chikkapattanagere Gate, Kadur Taluk, Chikkamagalur District, at that time, driver of Bolero Car bearing Reg. No.KA-18-Z-3827 being driven by its driver at a very high speed in rash and negligent manner came from opposite direction by overtaking another vehicle to extreme right side and dashed against him, due to the forced impact, Lohith was thrown out of his motor cycle and sustained fatal injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was taken to Kadur Government hospital,
thereafter shifted to Shimoga Max Hospital, wherein duty doctors referred him to higher hospitals at Bengaluru, wherein he succumbed to the injuries while on the way to the hospital towards Bengaluru on 09.11.2023 at about SCCH 5 3.00 a.m. Thereafter body was shifted to Kadur Government hospital, wherein post moretm was conducted and body was handed over to the petitioners, who performed cremation, funeral,
obsequies and other ceremonies, for which they have spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/-.

3. At the time of accident, deceased/Lohith was aged about 24 years, doing plumbing and electrical works and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m. Petitioner No.1 is mother, petitioner No.2 is father and petitioner No.3 is sister of the deceased/Lohith.
Due to sudden and untimely demise of the deceased, petitioners are undergoing mental agony and put to great financial inconvenience, they are finding difficulty to eakout their daily life.

Out of the said accident, crime No.304/2023 is Nethramma vs Indramma on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197280790/
2 registered against the driver of the Bolero Car bearing Reg. No.KA-18-Z-3827 before the Kadur Police.
SCCH 5
Respondent No.1 is R.C.Owner and respondent No.2 is insurer of the said car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

So that, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.
On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 / insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied the entire case of the petitioners.

This respondent submitted that, the alleged offending vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and petitioners have lodged belated complaint before jurisdictional police by wrongly implicating the alleged offending vehicle.

Further submitted that, deceased/rider of the motor cycle was riding without valid insurance policy and fitness certificate at the time of accident, hence police have filed charge sheet against owner of the motor cycle SCCH 5 under Sec.192 and 196 of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, R.C.Owner and insurer of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-EE-8375 was not impleaded as party, hence petition is not maintainable for non-joinder of necessary parties.

There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act and also admitted issuance of poilicy bearing No.2414813122P112104060 in favour of Shravana Kumar S. in respect of private car bearing Reg. No.KA-18-Z-3827 and his liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further denied age, occupation and income of the deceased.
Compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant and imaginary one.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following:
SCCH 5 ::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioners prove that, deceased Lohith, S/o. Nagaraja K.T. died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 08.11.2023 at about 6.20 p.m. near Kalavase Farm, NH-173 road, Chikapattanagere Gate, Kadur Taluk, Chikkamagalur due to rash and negligent driving of Bolero Car bearing Reg. No.KA-18-Z-3827 and dashed against the deceased motor cycle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so how much and from whom?
3.
What order or award?
6. In order to prove their case, Petitioner No.1/mother of the deceased herself deposed her evidence as PW-1 and exhibited 12 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, Administrative officer of respondent No.2 is SCCH 5 examined as RW-1 and marked 2 documents as per Ex.R.1 and Ex.R.2 and closed his evidence.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and the records those were marked i.e., FIR, complaint, crime details form, seizure mahazar, IMV Report, inquest report, P.M.Report, Sec.133 notice, reply and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioners about causing of the accident dated 08.11.2023 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
10.
Per contra, the Administrative Officer of respondent No.2 is examined as RW-1 and exhibited authorization letter marked as Ex.R.1 and copy of policy marked as Ex.R.2.
Further except oral evidence, respondent No.2 has not taken any endeavors to disprove SCCH 5 the petitioners case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Hence I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioners about death of Lohith K.N. out of the accident held on 08.11.2023 at about 6.20 p.m. when he was riding motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-EE-8375 near Kalavase Farm, NH-173 Road, Chikkapattanagere Gate, Kadur Taluq, Chikkamagalur District.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioners.
11. The police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of the car.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioners, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioners have proved the above issue No.1 in their favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
SCCH 5 12. Issue No.2:-
As per the case of the petitioners, deceased/Lohith K.N. was aged about 24 years as on the date of accident.

For proof of age of the deceased, they have produced copy of aadhar card of the deceased marked as Ex.P.11, wherein date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 08.07.1999,
the alleged accident was occurred on 08.11.2023.

Accordingly relying on aadhar card, age of the deceased is considered about 25 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 18 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

To prove the said facts, they have furnished notarized copy of aadhar card of petitioner No.1 to 3 marked as Ex.P.11 it reveals that, they are legal representatives of the deceased/Lohith K.N., hence they will become dependents of the deceased.

15. As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the deceased is bachelor, then 1/2 of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/2 of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.
SCCH 5 16.

In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, the Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, an addition of 40% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged below 40 years, in case of fixed salary employee.

multiplier of 18 is 12 x 18 applied 18.
Further petitioner No.1 and 2 being the parents and petitioner No.3 being sister of the deceased are entitled for Rs.20,000/- each towards filial consortium.
Further they are entitled for loss of estate of Rs.15,000/- and also they are entitled for funeral expenses for an amount of Rs.15,000/-.

with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
21.

During the course of arguments, petitioner counsel Sri. MM vehemently argued that, it is a case of death of 22 years old and he is unmarried and prays to deduct 50% of his income towards personal expenses and also counsel argued that, charge sheet has been filed against the offending vehicle under Sec.196 of M.V.Act for non having insurance and entire negligence is on the the insured vehicle and prays to allow the petition.
22.

Per contra, Sri.KRS respondent No.2 counsel argued that, liability is undisputed and without SCCH 5 insurance policy he has driven the vehicle and only owner is liable to pay compensation,
because he has not obtained insurance policy for the date of the accident to the offending vehicle and charge sheet is also filed against the owner of the vehicle and contributory negligence of 25%
can be imposed on the owner of the vehicle etc.,
23.
On perusal of entire papers, admittedly deceased Lohith K.N. is 3rd party to the offending vehicle as well as respondent No.2.
So the arguments of the respondent No.2 counsel for imposing of contributory negligence at the rate of 25% on owner is not at all helpful to the case in hand.

Because on perusal of overall materials it clearly indicates to the court about death of Lohith out of the accident caused by the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-18-Z-3827 and admittedly said offending vehicle is insured with respondent No.2, as SCCH 5 such respondent No.2 is alone liable to pay compensation as stated supra.
Accordingly any amount of arguments addressed by the respondent No.2 counsel have not support his case.

24. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Bolero car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-EE-8375 has issued insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 vide policy bearing No.2414813122P112104060 which is valid from 19.02.2023 to 18.02.2024, the alleged accident was occurred on 08.11.2023, hence as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

So that,
respondent No.2/insurer of the car is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

::ORDER

The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.23,95,800/- (Rupees Twenty Three Lakhs Ninety Five Thousand Eight Hundred Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio 50:40:10 in the award amount.

The petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be SCCH 5 kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
